models: Ollama-hosted model (not named in the page I verified)

incidents.title: Vibe-coded PowerShell script maps Active Directory during intrusion
incidents.targets: Victim organization accessed via compromised remote credentials over RDP
incidents.outcome: AD users, computers, groups and trusts enumerated and zipped for exfiltration; s5cmd and SharpShares followed.
incidents.confidenceReason: Huntress rebuilt the script from logs and cites chatbot-style title, unedited placeholder host and over-engineered fallbacks.
incidents.summary: During a live intrusion the actor ran a script titled as a finished chatbot debugging session, with a leftover placeholder hostname. Huntress argues behavior-based detection is needed because such scripts are unique each time.
incidents.quote: The script, enthusiastically titled "100% Working AD Information Gathering Script - FULLY FIXED"
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Huntress has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

harness.note: AI used as an assistant, no agent harness

incidents.title: Hong Kong syndicate used deepfake portraits on lost ID cards to pass bank facial-recognition checks
incidents.targets: Online banking facial-recognition checks (19 accounts, about HK$220,000)
incidents.outcome: Bank facial-recognition checks were passed with altered lost ID cards; members were arrested.
incidents.confidenceReason: The Hong Kong government's own press release states the syndicate used deepfake technology.
incidents.summary: A syndicate used deepfake technology to replace the portraits on lost identity cards and pass banks' facial-recognition checks.
incidents.quote: The syndicate used deepfake technology to replace the portraits on HKICs which had been reported as lost, and successfully passed the facial recognition verification of online banking systems, opened 19 bank accounts, and used those identity cards to apply for loans and credit cards, involving approximately HK$220,000.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Hong Kong Government has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: JadePuffer: LLM agent runs an entire extortion operation from Langflow exploit to data destruction
incidents.targets: Internet-facing Langflow instance, then an exposed MySQL and Alibaba Nacos production server
incidents.outcome: 1,342 Nacos configuration items encrypted with an unrecoverable ephemeral key; ransom note left; data not recoverable even if paid.
incidents.confidenceReason: The Register quoting Sysdig; Sysdig's basis is artifact inference: payloads with 'the kind of detailed annotations that ... LLM-generated code produces reflexively'. Sysdig's own JadePuffer post not cited.
incidents.summary: Sysdig says an LLM, not a human, drove the intrusion: exploit CVE-2025-3248, steal credentials, persist, attack the database and encrypt. It retried failed steps in real time. Primary Sysdig URL was not verified.
incidents.quote: gained initial access to an internet-facing Langflow instance

harness.note: Sysdig says an LLM agent drove the full intrusion; no framework named

incidents.title: JetBrains Marketplace AI plugins steal OpenAI and DeepSeek API keys
incidents.actor: Unknown publishers of seven vendor accounts
incidents.targets: Developers using JetBrains IDE AI assistant plugins
incidents.outcome: Users' AI API keys were harvested from about 70,000 installs and handed out in a paid tier.
incidents.confidenceReason: Aikido analyzed the plugins; it reaches us through AI Threat Watch.
incidents.summary: At least 15 JetBrains plugins posing as AI assistants sent users' OpenAI, DeepSeek and SiliconFlow API keys to an attacker server, whose paid tier gave out the harvested keys.
incidents.quote: Aikido found at least 15 plugins from seven vendor accounts that acted as AI assistants but sent users OpenAI, DeepSeek and SiliconFlow API keys over plain HTTP to an attacker server; a paid tier gave out harvested keys.
incidents.singleSourceReason: This operation reaches the ledger only through AI Threat Watch's record; the 2026-11-17 sweep found no other publisher.

incidents.title: Pro-Iran hackers abuse Meta's AI support assistant to seize Instagram accounts
incidents.confidenceReason: Krebs reports the defacements and that 'instructions began circulating on Telegram showing how to trick Meta's "AI support assistant"', citing 'a video released on Telegram claiming to show' it. No Meta confirmation is in the source. It rests on the attackers' own claim.
incidents.summary: Pro-Iran hackers seized Instagram accounts; the exploit appears to have involved chatting with Meta's AI support assistant in the account-recovery flow.
incidents.quote: A video released on Telegram by pro-Iran hackers claimed to document a remarkably simple exploit that appears to have involved using a VPN connection with an IP address that is in or near the target’s usual hometown, requesting a password reset for the account, and then choosing to chat with Meta’s AI support assistant.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Krebs on Security has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

sources.title: Pro-Iran hackers abuse Meta's AI support assistant to seize Instagram accounts

incidents.title: PRC-nexus UNC6508 deploys a local open-weight LLM inside compromised cloud environments
incidents.targets: Academic, medical and military research institutions in North America
incidents.outcome: The actor co-opted victims' compute to run its own model.
incidents.confidenceReason: GTIG, which investigated the intrusions, states the actor deployed the model inside compromised environments.
incidents.summary: PRC-nexus UNC6508 deployed a local open-weight LLM inside compromised cloud environments to power its operations while avoiding commercial API monitoring. GTIG reported the espionage campaign in June 2026; the LLM detail is from its September 2026 report.
incidents.quote: By using a local, open-weight model deployed in compromised infrastructure, UNC6508 is able to avoid commercial AI API monitoring, while co-opting victim compute resources.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Google Threat Intelligence Group has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.
